purpose: Classify easements, rights of way and related registered property rights while separating documentary registration, legal existence, scope and physical use.
legal_distinctions: A registered entry and the underlying instrument may need to be read together to understand the right.
A title plan does not automatically define every practical aspect of an easement or right of way.
Physical use of a route is not by itself proof of the legal right being claimed.
Prescription is distinct from creation by deed or registration and requires its own legal analysis.
An easement/right of way can involve both a benefit to one property and a burden on another.
A court declaration or judgment is distinct from the underlying registration step.
evidence_requirements: current folios and title plans where relevant
underlying deed or filed instrument where relevant
court order or declaration where applicable
official_routes: Tailte Éireann Land Registry records and forms
Registry of Deeds search where applicable
Courts Service where a judicial declaration or dispute route is relevant
guardrails: Never infer a right of way solely from physical use.
Never infer the full scope of an easement from a map alone.
Never treat a Registry of Deeds search as proof of the deed's complete legal effect.
Never collapse prescription, deed creation and registration into one pathway.
Never state that a disputed right exists without sufficient legal and factual evidence.
